main_decision: Stop treating down-only polishing as a complete3x strategy. Use bounded down prototypes to establish a transferable engine, then attack both GEMMs and larger token-tile reuse; preserve current Marlin fallback until an entire reviewed expert path wins.

attribution_method.procedure: Select cat=kernel; remove five explicit128MiBcacheflush FillFunctor kernels; pair ascending-time Marlin launches as gate/up then down, consistent with source call order. Sum remaining kernel durations; do not use these as clean latency benchmarks.
attribution_method.limitations: Historical single-fixture profiler shares omit host/launch gaps and do not establish present clean critical-path fractions. Amdahl values are conditional attribution models, not measured speedups. Gather fresh stage attribution in any next architecture test.

amdahl.primary_summary: Down-only infinite speed gives~1.46–1.48x; gate/up alone also below3x. Equal acceleration of both GEMMs requires~3.44–4.04x across fourprimary traces if other cost fixed.
amdahl.prefill_summary: M3012/M16384 both-GEMM requirement~3.35x; down-only cap~1.48x. A narrow8token kernel cannot be assumed efficient here.
amdahl.smallest_shape: M1 has~20.24%other work; both-GEMM acceleration alone would need~6.09x for per-shape3x. This is not a new requirement that everyshape individually reach3x; original aggregation/gates govern.
